cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Hello Dr Green - I’m here to talk to you about my work placement.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR: Oh yes, it's Holly, isn't it? HOLLY: Yes.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR: So, which work placement have you chosen?

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY: I decided to go for the Orion Stadium placement.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: The event I'll be managing is one where I'm helping to set up a sports competition for

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: primary school children. TUTOR: Yup.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: That's always a popular placement — even though it can be tougher than you think working

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: with children.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY: I know, but it's the fresh air that attracts me — organising something indoors

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: doesn't have the same appeal, even though it might be fun.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR: OK, so obviously safety's going to be one of your key concerns for this event.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Yes, I've already thought about that.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: I'll need to make sure none of the equipment's damaged.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR: Ah well, you'll be working with schools, so the equipment will be their

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: responsibility. However, the grounds and what goes on there will be yours.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY: Oh I see - that'll include keeping everyone within the boundary once they're in

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: their kit and on the field?

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR: Exactly — you'll need to inspect areas like changing rooms as well for anything

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: someone can trip over, but your main priority will be not to lose anyone! HOLLY: Right.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: I'll need staff to help with that. TUTOR: And don't forget about the spectators.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY: Mmm.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: I was thinking that many of them will be parents, who could help run the event.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR: I wouldn't rely on that.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: They'll be more interested in filming their children than volunteering.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY: I'll need to make sure they don't interfere with events doing that!

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: ‘ila 1718867188 TUTOR And that's not always easy, especially when a proud parent's trying

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: to get a snap of their child and you want them to move elsewhere. HOLLY OK.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: What about the scheduling?

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR With sporting events there are all sorts of things that can alter the timetable —

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: like rain, for instance — though so far, we've always been lucky with that.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY Yeah, and I was thinking about what to do if someone got hurt as well.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: I know that last year that caused a terrible delay.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR You have to be prepared for such things. HOLLY Oh.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: What if a match ends in a draw — do you let the teams keep going until someone wins?

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR That'll be up to you — and again, you need to plan for it. HOLLY Right.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR Now, the aim of your work placement is to give you the opportunity to develop the

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: skills that an events manager needs. So, let's talk about those a bit.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY Well, I think my communication skills are pretty good.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: I can talk on the phone to people and book venues and that kind of thing.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR Good - just remember it isn't only about what you say.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: If you meet someone ace-to-face and want to persuade them to be a sponsor, for example ...

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY Oh, I'll dress up for that! Sure. TUTOR Good.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Let's go on to think about your organisational skills.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: You're working in a very people-based industry and that means things won't always go to

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: plan. HOLLY guess it's being prepared to make changes that matters.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR That's right.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: You may have to make an on-the-spot change to a timetable because of a problem you hadn't

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: anticipated ... HOLLY ... just do it! OK. TUTOR How's your time management these days?

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY "m working on it — I'm certainly better when I have a deadline, which is why this

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: work suits me. TUTOR Yes, but it's how you respond as that deadline approaches!

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY know I've got to look calm even if I'm in a panic.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR: Just think to yourself — no one must know I’m under pressure.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY: Yeah — even though I’m multi-tasking like crazy!

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR: Another skill that events managers need is creativity.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Often your client has what we call the 'big picture' idea, but it's up to the events

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: manager to think of all the fine points that go to making it work.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY Right, so I need to listen carefully to that idea and then fill in all the gaps.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR That's right.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: And you'll have a team working under you, so another key skill is leadership.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Your team may have lots of ideas too, but you've got to make the ultimate choices.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Do we have refreshments inside or out, for example?

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY Isn't it better to be democratic?

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR It's a nice idea, but you have the ultimate responsibility.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: So, believe in what you think best.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: Be prepared to say ‘yes’, that's a good idea but it won't work here.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY I see what you mean.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: What about the networking side of things?

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: I know it's an area that a lot of students worry about because we don't have much

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: experience to offer others.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR But even without it — you can still be an interesting person with useful ideas.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: And the more people you impress, the better.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY I guess that will help me when I apply for a real job.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: TUTOR Exactly — think ahead — remember what your ambitions are and keep them in mind.

cues.speaker: HOLLY
cues.text: HOLLY Definitely.
